text: The Honda Battle of the Bands (often abbreviated as The Honda or HBOB) is an annual marching band exhibition in the United States that showcases performances by bands from historically black colleges and universities (HBCUs). Sponsored by the American Honda Motor Company, the Invitational Showcase was held in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia from late January 2003 to 2020. In February 2023, Alabama State University in Montgomery, Alabama was selected as the first HBCU campus to host the in-person event, marking a significant shift in location. Since 2023, the event has moved to new venues, with the 2025 showcase taking place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, making it the first time the event was held on the West Coast. The Honda Battle of the Bands Celebration Tour occurs between September and November at regular season football games, though the term "Honda Battle of the Bands" typically refers only to the invitational showcase, which began in 2003. Despite the name, Honda's "battle" is not a competition with a declared winner; instead, bands compete for audience and community favor. The event is one of the most popular collegiate marching band events in the nation, drawing over 50,000 fans annually. The program includes two components: a Voting Process from September to October and the Invitational Showcase. The first band is selected by popular vote, while the next three are chosen from three instrument categories—128 instruments or fewer, 129 to 160, and 161 or more—using a weighted vote from institution presidents, band directors, and an online opinion poll, with presidents and directors not allowed to vote for their own institutions. The final four bands are selected by American Honda and the Urban Sports & Entertainment Group based on, but not limited to, the voting results. A total of eight bands are invited to perform halftime routines in front of 50,000+ fans. The event was created in 2003 to celebrate, support, and recognize the excellence of Black college marching bands and the unique academic experience at HBCUs. Honda annually awards more than $205,000 in grants to participating bands and hosts a HBCU recruitment fair before the showcase. In 2018, the event was on a one-year hiatus in 2019 due to Super Bowl LIII being held in Atlanta; it resumed in 2020. In 2020, Honda announced a one-year pause in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with the in-person event cancelled again in 2021, though a virtual event was likely held in 2022. In 2022, Honda announced the return of the in-person event in 2023 and released a four-part docuseries celebrating HBCU culture and bands on February 26, 2022. In November 2023, Honda announced a one-year hiatus in 2024 due to the Toad Bowl Game being held there and not being relocatable. In April 2024, Honda confirmed the return of the event in February 2025 at SoFi Stadium in Southern California. The event's coordinates are 33°57′11″N 118°20′20″W / 33.953°N 118.339°W / 33.953; -118.339.
